_doc: THE Configs ▸ General / Configs ▸ About rule of the fleet (#1352, v2), read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-configs-pages-guard.py (step of nav-shape-guard.yml, mutation-tested by 1_cicd/src/scripts/test/configs-pages-guard.test.sh) and by libs/ui-nav-bars/fleet-configs.gradle at build time (perm_why, diagnostics, origin_label). Every app except Cloud SuperApp has two pages under Configs. General is ONE page: at the top a launcher-style grid of anchors (an icon tile with the section's name under it, four per row) scrolling to its sections on the same page: Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection with a prominent Grant all that walks every missing grant), Update (every app by default: installed version and build, Check for updates against the app's Cloud Store release, latest build, Update handed to Cloud Store, release notes), Battery, Storage/backup, Notifications, UI with the nav mode card, Language, then the app's own Configs. Every settings screen is opened through libs:perms. About is EXTENSIVE: name, icon, tagline, a long description, features, screens, a quick guide, data and privacy (privacy text, the stores from the fleet-config manifest, backups, crash/analytics libs), permissions and why (build.json::perms + perm_why), backend services with private mesh URLs, related fleet apps with Open buttons, version / build sha / build date / package, source repo, licence, origin, upstream and credits, the changelog (the commits of the app's folder), support and debug links, and the Cloud Store and Cloud SuperApp sections with Open buttons. Both are drawn ONCE in libs:ui-nav-bars (package fleetconfigs); an app drawn with Views, a WebView, Tauri or an upstream fork starts FleetConfigsActivity. Each app declares its sections and the hand-written About text in build.json::configs_pages; nothing per app is written in Kotlin.
_doc_rules: G0 the lib still carries the pages, the grid, the Update section, the extended About, the scaffold entries, the Views/WebView activity, the build-time resolver and the two fleet texts (lib.must_hold); FleetConfigs.REQUIRED_SECTIONS equals general_required; libs:perms carries the asked-store version (perms.ask_store_version) and Grant all's walk. G1 every app (a[acd]_*/build.json) that is not exempt declares configs_pages with general and about. G2 general.sections lists every general_required id once, only ids from general_required + general_optional + general_default. G3 about carries every about_declared field and meets about_min (tagline length, description, features, screens {name, what}, guide steps, privacy, related {app, why} naming real apps, backends {id, why} on a fleet_endpoints service with a mesh_dns, credits for an app whose licences/curated.json kind is in fork_kinds), every grant in build.json::perms has a why (about.perms_why or perm_why), the v1 field `what` is gone, and every about_derived field resolves. G4 the app REACHES the pages (scaffold_call or views_call in its sources) or is named in pending with a reason; a pending app that reaches them is stale. G5 every exempt / pending entry names a real app and has a reason of at least min_reason_chars.

origin_label.upstream-fork: Signed fork of an upstream open-source app
origin_label.patch-series: Upstream app with a series of fleet patches
origin_label.own-shell-over-gpl: Own shell over GPL upstream components

diagnostics._doc: What each crash / analytics library linked by an app records and where it goes; About lists the ones the app links (libs:crash always, through libs:core).
diagnostics.libs:crash: libs:crash: a crash report (stack trace, app version, device model) is saved on the phone and posted only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback.
diagnostics.libs:analytics: libs:analytics: opt-in usage events to the fleet's self-hosted Umami and Matomo; off until consent is given, and a refusal drops the queue.

perm_why._doc: The default reason each libs:perms catalogue grant is used, shown in About ▸ Permissions; an app overrides one in configs_pages.about.perms_why.
perm_why.notifications: Show alerts, progress and the status of background work.
perm_why.fine_location: Know the precise position for maps, tracking or location-tagged results.
perm_why.coarse_location: Know the approximate area for local results.
perm_why.background_location: Keep recording a track while the screen is off.
perm_why.nearby_wifi: Scan nearby Wi-Fi networks and devices.
perm_why.bt_connect: Connect to paired Bluetooth devices and headsets.
perm_why.camera: Take photos, record video or scan QR codes and documents.
perm_why.microphone: Record audio for voice input, calls or sound measurement.
perm_why.activity_recognition: Count steps and recognise walking, cycling or driving.
perm_why.body_sensors: Read heart rate and other body sensors.
perm_why.exact_alarm: Ring alarms and reminders at the exact minute.
perm_why.contacts_read: Read contacts to show names and reach people.
perm_why.calendar_read: Read calendar events to show what is due.
perm_why.phone_state: Know whether a call is active and read the phone's call state.
perm_why.media_images: Show the photos on the phone.
perm_why.media_video: Show the videos on the phone.
perm_why.media_audio: Play and share music and audio files.
perm_why.all_files: Manage every file on shared storage (a file manager, a terminal, backups).
perm_why.install_unknown: Install fleet updates and companion APKs.
perm_why.usage_access: See which apps run and how much they are used.
perm_why.battery_opt: Keep background work alive under battery optimisation.
perm_why.overlay: Draw over other apps (floating windows, call screens).
perm_why.health_connect: Read and write health data through Health Connect.
perm_why.accessibility: Fill passwords into other apps (autofill through accessibility).

pending._doc: Apps that declare configs_pages (held by G1-G3) but do not reach the pages yet. Wiring means linking libs:ui-nav-bars (with bottomnav, ui-icons, theme-background, perms) and calling FleetConfigsMenu( (Compose) or FleetConfigsEntries.addTo( / FleetConfigsActivity.intent( (Views, forks) from the app's own menu. Delete an entry in the commit that wires the app (the guard fails a stale one).
